title: Anaphylaxis
sources: Critical Vector — EM Pocket Guide: Anaphylaxis (ACAAI 2024)
Joint Task Force Anaphylaxis Practice Parameter 2023 update

changelog.change: Initial entry — diagnostic criteria, the numbered treatment sequence, refractory management, and observation/disposition.

summary: Epinephrine IM is always first-line and has no contraindication in anaphylaxis — every minute of delay increases mortality. Antihistamines and steroids do NOT treat anaphylaxis; they are adjuncts only. Give epinephrine on clinical suspicion, before the picture is complete.

body.text: Do not give an antihistamine first and 'watch'. Epinephrine 0.3–0.5 mg IM in the lateral thigh, repeated every 5–15 min as needed, is the treatment.

items: Acute skin/mucosal involvement PLUS respiratory compromise, OR hypotension, OR end-organ dysfunction.
Two or more body systems involved after likely allergen exposure (skin, respiratory, cardiovascular, GI, CNS).
Hypotension alone after a known allergen exposure.
1 — Epinephrine 0.3–0.5 mg IM (1:1000) into the lateral thigh; repeat q5–15 min as needed. No contraindication.
2 — Supine (or left lateral if vomiting / pregnant) with legs raised; high-flow O2; two large-bore IVs; 1–2 L crystalloid for hypotension.
3 — Diphenhydramine 25–50 mg IV — adjunct only, never a substitute for epinephrine (± an H2 blocker).
4 — Methylprednisolone 125 mg IV — aimed at biphasic-reaction prevention; not an acute treatment and evidence is weak.
5 — Refractory: epinephrine infusion 0.05–0.5 mcg/kg/min; add glucagon 1 mg IV if the patient is on a beta-blocker.
6 — Observe ≥ 4–8 h; 24 h if severe or high biphasic risk. Discharge with two epinephrine auto-injectors, an action plan, and allergy follow-up.

body.text: Refractory hypotension or stridor despite IM epinephrine → start the infusion early and prepare for a difficult airway (angioedema). Persistent bronchospasm: nebulised salbutamol. Persistent upper-airway oedema: nebulised epinephrine and early intubation by the most experienced operator.
